name: answer_quality_v1
purpose: Real-model answer-quality evaluation (brief: at least 15 questions). Questions are referenced by ID from eval/questions.jsonl and never copied or edited here.

authorship.note: Every chosen question carries a 'User idea N' note in questions.jsonl; several were narrowed or reframed. The owner confirms authorship before the results are reported.

q06: tokenization is a barrier to true end-to-end models
q07: the decoder adds a third sub-layer that attends over the encoder output
decoder self-attention is masked so a position cannot attend to later positions
encoder-decoder attention: queries from the previous decoder layer, keys and values from the encoder output
q08: sinusoids chosen so the model can attend by relative position and/or extrapolate to longer sequences
learned positional embeddings gave nearly identical results
q09: 80 ms from one Mimi frame at 12.5 Hz plus 80 ms of acoustic delay gives 160 ms
below the roughly 230 ms average gap in natural conversation
q10: a stage is encoder, dynamic chunking into a main network, dechunking and decoder
the main network can itself be an H-Net, so stages nest
q12: with Inner Monologue: 26.6 Web Questions, 62.3 Llama Questions, 22.8 Audio TriviaQA
q13: 2-stage H-Net 55.5 vs BPE Transformer 53.3 at GPT-3 Large compute
55.5 matches the Transformer at GPT-3 XL compute
q14: the Transformer used fixed subword vocabularies (byte-pair encoding, about 37000 shared tokens for English-German, and/or a 32000 word-piece vocabulary for English-French)
H-Net reads raw bytes and learns its segmentation with dynamic chunking

labels.correct_full_cited: Answerable; an answer was delivered; every required element is present and correct; no false claim; every factual sentence is fully supported by the passages it cites.
labels.correct_partially_cited: Answerable; an answer was delivered; every required element is present and correct; no false claim; at least one factual sentence is only partly supported or unsupported by its cited passages, although the claim is true according to the papers.
labels.partially_correct: Answerable; an answer was delivered; no false claim; at least one required element is missing (including an answer that says part of it is not stated). Citation support is recorded per sentence.
labels.factually_wrong: An answer was delivered that contains at least one false claim or a wrong paper attribution; for an unanswerable question, any delivered answer that invents or implies the missing information or accepts a false premise.
labels.correct_refusal: Unanswerable; the reply refuses or says the information is not in the retrieved passages, and invents nothing. True, cited side facts are allowed (e.g. q21: H100 GPUs, count not stated). Answering only the answerable part without inventing the rest counts here and is noted in the rationale.
labels.false_refusal: Answerable; the reply is a refusal, whatever caused it (structural check, model declined, verifier rejection after redraft). The cause is recorded as a failure category, never as a correct outcome.
labels.not_run: No reply because the run stopped (budget, provider error, daily limit). Excluded from rates and reported separately.

sentence_level.note: Graded for every draft, delivered or rejected, by reading the cited passage text stored in the raw record. The verifier's decision per sentence comes from the raw record and is kept in separate columns.

grading: Assistant pre-grades every question, draft and sentence (label: assistant_graded); the owner confirms or changes each grade. No LLM judge and no judging API calls.

per_class: answerable (10): correct_full_cited, correct_partially_cited, partially_correct, factually_wrong, false_refusal
also: verifier false acceptances and false rejections on graded drafts
tokens per question and per delivered answer
metrics.intervals: counts with Wilson 95% intervals; n is small
